name: Rex Smeal Park
note: Park: palm-shaded foreshore park in Port Douglas, a sunset picnic spot over the Coral Sea (tourism board list).

name: Spring Creek Falls
note: Waterfall: walk-in waterfall and waterhole near Port Douglas, named in the tourism board's waterfall list.

name: Mowbray Falls
note: Waterfall: rainforest waterfall and walk on the Mowbray River near Port Douglas, named by the tourism board.

name: Cassowary Falls
note: Waterfall: rainforest falls and swimming hole in the Daintree area, named by the tourism board in its waterfall and day-tour lists.

name: Wildlife Habitat Port Douglas
note: Wildlife park: Port Douglas wildlife sanctuary with cassowaries, birds and crocodile encounters.

name: Noah Beach
note: Beach: Cape Tribulation beach where campers pitch tents on the sand (tourism board list). Named Noah's Beach in the source.

name: Newell Beach
note: Beach: small beach village 20 minutes north of Port Douglas with fish and chips and Island Point sunsets.

name: Thala Beach Nature Reserve
note: Nature reserve: beachfront ecolodge reserve and coconut plantation about 10 minutes from Port Douglas.

name: Flagstaff Hill Lookout
note: Viewpoint: lookout platform above Four Mile Beach for sunrise and sunset views over the Coral Sea.

name: Cape Tribulation Boardwalk
note: Walk: short boardwalk and lookouts at Cape Tribulation where rainforest meets the reef coast (tourism board list).

name: Isabella Falls
note: Waterfall: swimming falls on the Cooktown to Lakefield road, named in the Cape York drive itinerary.

name: Elim Beach
note: Beach: Cape Bedford beach near Hope Vale with coloured sand cliffs, a named optional detour.

name: Cape Bedford
note: Headland: cape reached through Hope Vale on the way to Elim Beach, named in the Cape York itinerary.

name: Coen
note: Town: small historic Cape York town with a post office, a hotel and a free camp at The Bend nearby.

name: The Bend
note: Campsite: free bush campsite and Coen River swimming spot a few kilometres from Coen.

name: Bramwell Station
note: Station stay: historic cattle station on the Cape York road with camping, a bar and live entertainment, a popular stop.

name: Moreton Telegraph Station
note: Historic site: restored Overland Telegraph repeater station on the Wenlock River with walks for birdwatching.

name: Punsand Bay
note: Beach: bay near Seisia, 5 km from The Tip, where the northernmost-point walk starts.

name: The Tip (Northernmost Point of the Australian Continent)
note: Landmark: Pajinka, the northernmost point of mainland Australia, reached by a walk over sand from Punsand Bay; no wiki title set (the article may be Pajinka, to check).

name: Fruit Bat Falls
note: Waterfall: scenic picnic and swim stop on the Old Telegraph Track near the Jardine River crossing.

name: Twin Falls (Cape York)
note: Waterfall: picnic and swim stop on the Old Telegraph Track south of the Jardine River; the wiki title needs checking for disambiguation.

name: Elliot Falls
note: Waterfall: picnic and swim stop on the Old Telegraph Track near the Jardine River.

name: Old Telegraph Track
note: Track: historic 4WD route along the old telegraph line to the Tip; pin at the midpoint of the route, not a trailhead.

name: Chilli Beach
note: Beach: east coast Cape York beach near Portland Roads, named as an optional detour with Iron Range.

name: Portland Roads
note: Coastal locality: birdwatching and fishing base on the east coast of Cape York, named in the itinerary.

name: Lockhart River
note: Town: Aboriginal community on the east coast known for its vibrant art, named in the itinerary.

name: Wik and Kugu Arts and Crafts Centre
note: Gallery: Indigenous art centre in Aurukun on the western Cape, a visitor stop for local art.

name: Cooktown Botanic Gardens
note: Gardens: one of Queensland's oldest regional botanic gardens (1878) with a native plant collection.

name: Nature's Powerhouse
note: Visitor centre: Cooktown complex with the Vera Scarth-Johnson botanical art gallery, exhibitions and a cafe.

name: Milbi Wall (The Story Wall)
note: Monument: public mural wall in Cooktown acknowledging the first recorded contact between Cook's crew and the Guugu Yimithirr people.

name: Little Annan Gorge
note: Gorge: swimming hole on the Annan River near Cooktown, inside Annan River National Park.

name: Trevathan Falls
note: Waterfall: stunning waterfall just south of Cooktown, named in the regional tourism listings.

name: Wujal Wujal Falls
note: Waterfalls: sacred falls around the Wujal Wujal Kuku-Yalanji community near the Bloomfield, named by the tourism board for its many falls.

name: Gamaay Dreaming Track
note: Walking track: Indigenous-guided walk through tropical landscapes from coastal terrain, named in the regional tourism listings; location to confirm.

name: Split Rock (Quinkan Rock Art)
note: Rock art site: Quinkan rock art gallery near Laura that visitors can explore independently.

name: Giant Horse Gallery
note: Rock art site: Quinkan art gallery on the Mulligan Highway detour to Laura, named in the Cairns to Cape York itinerary.

name: Jarramali Rock Art Gallery
note: Rock art gallery: 20,000-year-old paintings on a sandstone escarpment, visited by tour from Laura; the gallery is the spot, the operator's tours are the way in.

name: Laura
note: Town: small Lakeland settlement on the Mulligan Highway, base for the Quinkan rock art sites and the Laura Quinkan Dance Festival.

name: Mackay Cay
note: Reef cay: green turtle swimming spot on the outer reef reached by reef boat from Port Douglas.

name: Agincourt Reef
note: Reef: outer Great Barrier Reef pontoon site reached by boat from Port Douglas, with snorkelling and an underwater observatory.

name: Port Douglas Sunday Markets
note: Market: weekly Sunday market at the headland park in Port Douglas (one day a week; judged against the market rule).

name: Bump Track
note: Mountain bike track: original link road between Port Douglas and the Atherton Tablelands, a self-guided ride.

name: CREB Track
note: 4WD track: off-road route near Port Douglas, open only when weather allows; a track, not a destination.

name: Mason's Waterhole
note: Swimming hole: safe rainforest waterhole on the Mossman River system, named by the tourism board.

name: Daintree Estates Chocolate
note: Farm: cocoa farm and chocolate maker in the Daintree area with tastings (a farm visit, operator).

name: Cape Trib Fruit Farm
note: Farm: tropical fruit farm at Cape Tribulation with rare fruit tastings (a farm visit, operator).

name: Coffee World Experience
note: Museum: coffee and tea exhibit at Coffee Works, Mareeba, on the Cairns to Cooktown route.

name: Mount Molloy
note: Town: small Tablelands town on the Mulligan Highway route to Cooktown, a passing stop with a historic streetscape.
